# Compose


Compose is iii's catalog-and-stack workflow. A repository may have one root
`worker-compose.yaml` containing release definitions and named stacks. This is
separate from the public `iii.worker.yaml` contract: `iii worker add ./path`
continues to support manifest-based local development, while release systems
compile the root catalog and never read those manifests.

## Commands

```bash
iii compose validate --file worker-compose.yaml
iii compose validate --file worker-compose.yaml --stack default
iii compose descriptor --file worker-compose.yaml --worker my-worker --source-sha "$GIT_SHA" --output -
iii compose descriptor-index --file worker-compose.yaml --source-sha "$GIT_SHA" --compiler-sha "$COMPILER_SHA" --output-dir .release
iii compose --file worker-compose.yaml --up
iii compose logs --file worker-compose.yaml --container my-worker
```

`validate` is offline and strict: unknown and duplicate fields fail. It compiles every catalog
worker into a normalized `PackageDescriptor`, validates local paths, reads the version from the
declared package manifest, and checks the selected stack DAG.

The engine exposes the same lifecycle through `compose::validate {path}`,
`compose::up {path, stack?, wait?}`, and `compose::down {path, stack?}`. Paths resolve on the
Compose daemon host.

## Root shape

```yaml
workers:
  my-worker:
    source:
      path: workers/my-worker
      package_manifest: package.json
    artifact:
      kind: javascript-bundle
      workspace_root: .
      runtime: {name: node, version: 22.20.0}
      package_manager: {name: pnpm, version: 11.13.1}
      lockfile: pnpm-lock.yaml
      install_command: [pnpm, install, --frozen-lockfile]
      build_command: [pnpm, run, build]
      include: [dist/bundle/index.mjs]
    runtime:
      exec: [node, ./dist/bundle/index.mjs]
      base_image: docker.io/library/node:22.20.0-slim@sha256:<64-hex-digest>
      resources: {cpu: 2, memory_mib: 2048}
    registry:
      description: Example worker
      license: Apache-2.0
      tags: [example]
      dependencies: {}
      publish: true
    validation:
      interface: required
stacks:
  default:
    namespace: example
    containers:
      worker:
        worker: catalog://my-worker
        start_after: []
```

The root accepts only `workers` and `stacks`. A stack accepts only `namespace` and `containers`.
A container accepts `worker`, optional `start_after`, and optional `config`. Use
`catalog://<slug>` for a worker defined in the same file and `package://<slug>` for a Registry
package. A map key is the worker identity; definitions do not repeat a `name` field.

## Artifact contracts

- `rust-binary` declares `binary`, `targets`, an exact Rust `toolchain`, and optional explicit
  frontend builds.
- `javascript-bundle` and `python-bundle` declare exact runtime/package-manager versions,
  workspace root, lockfile, install/build argv, and an explicit file list in `include`.
- `oci-image` declares `context`, `dockerfile`, and both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` platforms.

Bundle `include` entries are paths relative to `source.path`. The release archive preserves those
paths exactly; it never flattens or renames them. `runtime.exec` runs with the extracted archive as
`/workspace`, so its relative path must match the packaged layout. `install_command` and
`build_command` are release-build commands, not boot-time defaults. Any `runtime.prepare` command
runs inside the digest-pinned base image and must consume only packaged local content. A project
may explicitly include `iii.worker.yaml` for compatibility with `iii worker`; the descriptor-native
runtime does not inspect it.

## Release descriptors

`descriptor` writes one deterministic `release-descriptor` containing the normalized package,
its canonical SHA-256 digest, source SHA, and build units. `descriptor-index` compiles all workers
atomically into `release-descriptor-index.json` and `descriptors/<slug>.json`; downstream release
systems consume those bytes and do not reimplement Compose parsing or digest calculation.

Registry bundles contain only files enumerated by the descriptor plus compiler-owned descriptor
and digest sidecars installed by iii. Any explicitly packaged public manifest is compatibility
metadata, not a release-planning or descriptor-runtime input.
